Tenant isolation is server-enforced regardless of act-as state - non-admin users have no bypass. Tenants are safe whether platform staff use act-as or not.
Starting step-in (POST) is admin-only - non-admins get 403 `admin required`. GET (state) and DELETE (step out) answer any signed-in session.

Step-in belongs to an admin: if the account stops being one (the role column changes and it holds no global admin grant), its sessions stop using a step-in they still carry and answer in the account's own tenant again, while still counting as stepped-in for the direct-sign-in gates until DELETE /api/_auth/act_as clears it.

POST requires the admin's password as re-authentication. A stolen session cookie alone CANNOT start step-in; the attacker would also need the admin's password. Same pattern as /api/_auth/impersonate. Wrong-password attempts are logged.

Every step-in and step-out writes an audit row with action=`act_as_start`/`act_as_end`, `user_email` (the admin's), and `target_group_id` / `prior_group_id` in `new_values`. Query `_benmore_audit_log` for the governance trail.

Step-in DOES NOT downgrade the Role - `/_admin` and the admin management endpoints remain reachable while stepped in. If you want to mirror tenant-user UI exactly, gate the tenant-shell on `effective_group` (truthy) rather than on `role==='admin'`.
